figures.title: Dural sinuses and deep veins
figures.alt: Dural sinuses and deep veins on the complete published contrast-enhanced MR venography figure.
figures.caption: Sagittal and frontal MR venography projections retain seven numbered labels. The key follows the authors’ identifications.

figures.title: Basal veins
figures.alt: Basal veins on the complete published contrast-enhanced MR venography figure.
figures.caption: The red arrow identifies the basal veins on the supplied axial MRV panel. The article caption also mentions a sagittal plane, which is absent from this figure.

figures.title: Septal, thalamostriate and internal cerebral veins
figures.alt: Septal, thalamostriate and internal cerebral veins on the complete published contrast-enhanced MR venography figure.
figures.caption: The sagittal MRV view and circular axial inset retain the authors’ coloured arrows. The key follows the source caption.

figures.title: Superficial cortical veins · DSA
figures.alt: Lateral digital subtraction angiography with three original coloured arrows identifying the superficial middle cerebral, Trolard and Labbé veins.
figures.caption: The red arrow identifies the superficial middle cerebral vein, green identifies the superior anastomotic vein of Trolard, and blue identifies the inferior anastomotic vein of Labbé. This published DSA projection has no specified patient side.

figures.title: Right lateral-sinus filling defect · MRV
figures.alt: Right lateral-sinus filling defect · MRV in the complete original published figure.
figures.caption: Panels a and b are maximum-intensity projections. Panels c and d are selected source-slice images. The authors identify interruption of the proximal right lateral sinus and a filling defect suggesting thrombus. These panels provide selected views of the finding.

figures.title: Superior sagittal sinus thrombosis · CT
figures.alt: Superior sagittal sinus thrombosis · CT in the complete original published figure.
figures.caption: Panel a shows source-described superior sagittal sinus hyperdensity on nonenhanced CT. Panel b shows the empty delta sign on contrast-enhanced CT. The publication supplies selected sections, with no complete thrombus measurement or named venography protocol.

figures.title: Deep venous thrombosis with haemorrhagic infarction · MRI
figures.alt: Deep venous thrombosis with haemorrhagic infarction · MRI in the complete original published figure.
figures.caption: The authors describe a 27-year-old woman with deep venous thrombosis. Panel A shows absent flow signal in the internal cerebral veins (arrow) and vein of Galen. Panel B shows haemorrhagic venous infarction in the left caudate head and thalamus on susceptibility-weighted MRI. The source explicitly states that the straight sinus is not demonstrated.
labels: MR venogram with one orange arrow

figures.title: Jugular bulb landmarks · CBCT
figures.alt: Jugular bulb landmarks · CBCT in the original coronal image panels.
figures.caption: White outline marks the bulb. SUP, INF, LAT and MED are visible around it. Patient laterality is unspecified.

figures.title: Jugular bulb variants · CBCT
figures.alt: Jugular bulb variants · CBCT in the original coronal image panels.
figures.caption: The authors compare five jugular bulb variants on coronal cone-beam CT. In panel D, the dotted line marks the floor of the internal acoustic canal. These images illustrate anatomy and variants.

figures.title: Temporal horn enlargement with venous thrombosis
figures.alt: Four original panels. Left column axial FLAIR MRI. Right column nonenhanced axial CT from a different patient.
figures.caption: Panels A and B are FLAIR MRI from one patient with deep oedema and enlargement of both temporal horns. Panels C and D are nonenhanced CT from a different patient with a large left hemispheric haemorrhage and widening of the opposite temporal horn. The source provides selected sections.
labels: FLAIR MRI · bilateral temporal horn enlargement
Nonenhanced CT · left hemispheric haemorrhage and contralateral temporal horn widening

figures.title: Slender left transverse sinus and a separate thrombosis example
figures.alt: Four published panels with red arrows. Panels A to C are from one individual and D is from a separate patient.
figures.caption: In panels A and B the left transverse sinus is poorly seen. Contrast-enhanced T1 imaging in C shows a slender left transverse sinus in the same individual. The authors describe thrombosis of the left transverse and sigmoid sinuses and the upper internal jugular vein in the separate patient shown in D.
labels: Venographic projection in a separate patient with author-reported thrombosis

figures.title: Left lateral venous pathway on FLAIR
figures.alt: Three published axial FLAIR panels with white arrows on the patient’s left.
figures.caption: The authors describe abnormal FLAIR signal with loss of normal flow void along the distal left transverse sinus, sigmoid sinus and jugular bulb. Their MRI interpretation initially favoured slow flow. CT venography followed in the same patient.
labels: Abnormal FLAIR signal along the left lateral venous pathway in three axial panels. The caption gives the affected structures for the figure as a whole.

figures.title: Left lateral sinus and jugular bulb thrombosis on CT venography
figures.alt: Four published axial CT venogram panels with white arrows along the patient’s left lateral venous pathway.
figures.caption: In the same patient as Figure 1, the authors describe an occlusive filling defect along the distal left transverse sinus, sigmoid sinus and jugular bulb. The case text also describes involvement of the visualised left internal jugular vein. The selected panels have no separate jugular vein marker.
labels: Filling defect on four axial CT venogram panels. The authors identify the affected segments for the figure as a whole.

figures.title: Chronic thrombotic obstruction at the torcular
figures.alt: Six published panels with angiography, axial contrast-enhanced CT and MRI, and a colour venous reconstruction.
figures.caption: One patient with chronic venous outflow obstruction. The authors identify a chronic filling defect at the torcular on CTA and contrast-enhanced MRI. Angiography shows the venous pathway before and after stenting.
labels: Pre-stent venous-phase angiography. The authors describe narrowing in the torcular region.
Post-stent venous filling and the stent on angiography.
Axial CTA and contrast-enhanced MRI with the author-marked filling defect at the torcular.
Pre-stent 3D MR angiographic reconstruction with collateral drainage.

figures.title: Granulation, septation and tissue protrusion in transverse sinuses
figures.alt: Three angiograms above three MR panels. Each column shows a different patient.
figures.caption: Three patients illustrate distinct causes of transverse sinus narrowing. Each angiography panel is paired with the high-resolution MRI below it.
labels: Right transverse sinus hypoplasia and dominant left-sided narrowing. MRI shows the giant arachnoid granulation identified by the authors.
Right-sided narrowing and flow stratification. The authors report a right fibrous septation and left-sided arachnoid granulations.
Focal narrowing with cerebellar tissue protruding into an arachnoid granulation on MRI.

figures.title: Right high jugular bulb and sigmoid junction narrowing
figures.alt: Six published pretreatment panels with MR venography, temporal bone CT, and digital subtraction angiography.
figures.caption: All six panels are from one pulsatile tinnitus case. The authors describe a right high jugular bulb and narrowing where the right sigmoid sinus meets the internal jugular vein. The displayed case and the separate atlas model come from different sources.
labels: MR venography of the right high jugular bulb and the adjoining sigmoid-to-jugular narrowing.
Noncontrast CT. The authors identify a mastoid venous branch arising from the right sigmoid sinus.
Noncontrast CT showing the relationship of the high bulb to the inner ear.
Digital subtraction angiography showing the right jugular bulb and sigmoid junction.

figures.title: Thrombosis, compression and displacement after head trauma
figures.alt: Six published CT and MR panels showing four patterns of venous outflow compromise after head trauma.
figures.caption: Four representative trauma examples illustrate different ways a venous sinus can lose calibre or contrast. The authors distinguish intraluminal thrombus from external compression and displacement.
labels: CTV with absent right sigmoid contrast next to a fracture, interpreted as an occlusive thrombus. The left sigmoid sinus opacifies.
CTV with a left transverse filling defect and partial enhancement of the left transverse and sigmoid sinuses, interpreted as nonocclusive thrombosis.
Contrast-enhanced MRI showing subdural haematomas and narrowing of the right transverse sinus attributed to external compression.
CTV and noncontrast CT showing left transverse sinus displacement by a fracture-associated epidural collection.
